answer: Sybil attacks can be curbed using credit networks where transactional capacity flows through a river of staked collateral. Nodes broadcast state proofs over a decentralized whisper protocol, requiring peering agents to lock funds before exchanging tasks. An attacker incurs the verifiable financial cost of bonding scarce capital per identity. However, when deposit thresholds reach their zenith, honest agents with minimal liquidity are priced out of participation.
